items.title: Deadly strikes pound Middle East
items.description: Fresh explosions rock Tehran as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vows to intensify air strikes. Follow live.

items.title: Albanese's swift backing of US-Israel strikes tells of changed world
items.description: The speed at which the Albanese government backed the US-Israel operation is a tale of a changed world and a radically altered domestic environment.

items.title: Live: Government estimates 115,000 Australians in Middle East amid conflict
items.description: Foreign Minister Penny Wong says the government wants to wait and see if commercial flights to transport hubs in the Middle East restart before it considers repatriation flights for the 115,000 Australians estimated to be in the region. Follow live.

items.title: The Trump insult that pushed Marjorie Taylor Greene over the edge and out of MAGA
items.description: Many of Donald Trump's supporters wanted to send those implicated in Jeffrey Epstein's sex trafficking ring "off to the gallows", but then the president changed his mind about releasing the files. What followed was an unusual political manoeuvre, acts of immense bravery by survivors and a backflip by the president of the United States.

items.title: Russia captured their cities in 2022. This is what life looks like today
items.description: As Russian forces took control of their cities, millions of Ukrainians fled. Many still live as refugees, fearing they may never see their families or home towns again.

items.title: Mid-size cities lead property price charge as higher rates fail to slow buyers
items.description: Nationally, the median house price for all the capital cities is now more than $1 million.

items.title: 'Potentially catastrophic': Parents warn of safety risk without in-home childcare
items.description: In-home care provides services to about 1,000 families, but its viability is under threat because it is excluded from a government payment covering rising worker costs.

items.title: 'Something has changed': Is the era of AI job replacement here?
items.description: An entire retail and wholesale ecosystem has sprung from nothing in about a year, in a way that most people don't yet understand.

items.title: Men claiming to be council contractors chop down Bondi tree
items.description: Residents of a quiet street in Bondi are split after men wearing high-vis and wielding chainsaws allegedly illegally destroyed a tree.

items.title: Quick hits: Kerr makes difference, Fowler's class cameo and Lincoln cool in crisis
items.description: Sam Kerr makes the difference, Mary Fowler has a class cameo and Chloe Lincoln is cool in an injury crisis. Here are the quick hits from the Matildas' Asian Cup opener against the Philippines.

items.title: How a decades-old, 'daunting' act is deterring discrimination reporting
items.description: Australia's Disability Discrimination Act is decades old, with reform "well overdue". Removing the burden of proof could be the first step.

items.title: Live: Iran strikes set to rattle markets, oil and gold prices jump
items.description: Global markets are braced for the fallout from the outbreak of war in the Middle East. Follow today's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: History quiz: Can you work your way backward through these questions?
items.description: Where was MH370 heading, which Australian won our first Oscar and what was the world's first vampire movie?

items.title: Women carry bulk of the mental load, but men are active in one stage
items.description: While research has found mothers do more in all four stages of cognitive labour, there was one stage where men were more active than others.

items.title: 'Haven't looked back': How Max's move to the country changed his life
items.description: Moving to the country might sound idyllic to overstimulated and stressed-out city dwellers, but for Max and Courtney, it took some soul-searching to find their purpose and a place to really call home.

items.title: Should tick safety be as popular as 'slip, slop, slap'?
items.description: Australia's first death from a tick-induced allergy has sparked calls to ramp up awareness among the public and the medical profession.

items.title: Mum and son wait hours for police as thieves hit home for third time
items.description: Intruders break into a Toowoomba family's home in a post-midnight raid, forcing the woman and her 11-year-old son to lock themselves in a room after calling Triple Zero.

items.title: Qld on cyclone watch as rain drenches parts of state
items.description: Parts of Queensland have been drenched by more than 200 millimetres of rain in less than 24 hours — and there is more rain and potentially a cyclone on the way.

items.title: Punjabi school helping students and parents find community and connection
items.description: When the Virasati Punjabi School Geelong started five years ago, it had 15 students. Now, it has 53.

items.title: Flash flooding hits Mildura after 100mm of rain in 24 hours
items.description: Heavy rainfall causes flash flooding in Mildura as the city records its wettest March day.

items.title: Tasmania's locum nurse spend up 600 per cent from five years ago
items.description: State government spending on locum nurses continues to rapidly rise, despite repeated calls to build a more permanent workforce.

items.title: 'Pay with your privacy': Fears over OpenAI's move to insert ads in chatbot
items.description: The company said advertisements will appear at the bottom of answers and will be based on a user's current conversation.

items.title: Terminally ill grandmother tells productivity commissioner to 'remember my face'
items.description: The Australian government asked this woman how she felt about regional airfares. She didn't hold back.

items.title: The Nightcliff by-election is this weekend. Here is what you need to know
items.description: Residents living in Darwin's northern suburbs of Nightcliff, Rapid Creek and parts of Coconut Grove will be heading to the polls this Saturday to vote in a by-election. It comes after the former member for Nightcliff resigned in February.

items.title: WA transport industry wants tougher truck licensing model
items.description: Western Australia's transport industry is calling on the WA government to follow South Australia's lead in reforming its heavy vehicle licensing system, amid a "surge" in the number of road trains crossing the Nullarbor this week.
